# HTML response built from HTTP request data (Python)

`qualor:python/xss` · Issue · Severity: High · [CWE-79](https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html) · OWASP Top 10: [A05:2025 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2025/A05_2025-Injection/), [A03:2021 Injection](https://top10.owasp.org/2021/A03_2021-Injection/)

## What it finds

<!-- begin: what-it-finds -->
HTTP request data written into an HTML response without escaping:

- returned as the body of a Flask view, `make_response()` or `Response()`, a Django
  `HttpResponse`, a Starlette or FastAPI `HTMLResponse`, or a FastAPI path operation declared with
  `response_class=HTMLResponse`;
- wrapped in `Markup()`, `mark_safe()` or `SafeString()`, which switch escaping off, or used as the
  format string of `format_html()`.

Autoescaping templates (`render_template()`, Django's `render()`), JSON responses and escaped values
are not reported.
<!-- end: what-it-finds -->

## Why it matters

<!-- begin: why-it-matters -->
Markup in the value becomes part of the page. A value such as `<script>...</script>` runs in the
browser of everyone who opens the link or page: it can read what the user sees, act in their name
and steal data that scripts can reach.
<!-- end: why-it-matters -->

## Example

<!-- begin: example -->
**Noncompliant:** a Django view pastes the name into HTML.

```python
from django.http import HttpResponse


def hello(request):
    name = request.GET.get("name", "")
    return HttpResponse("<p>Hello, " + name + "</p>")
```

**Compliant:** `format_html()` escapes the value before inserting it.

```python
from django.http import HttpResponse
from django.utils.html import format_html


def hello(request):
    name = request.GET.get("name", "")
    return HttpResponse(format_html("<p>Hello, {}</p>", name))
```
<!-- end: example -->

## How to fix

<!-- begin: how-to-fix -->
- Render HTML through an autoescaping template: Flask's `render_template()`, Django's `render()`.
- Or escape the value: `markupsafe.escape()`, `html.escape()`, Django's `escape()` or
  `format_html("...{}...", value)`. For HTML that users may write, sanitise it with `nh3` or
  `bleach`.
- Where no HTML is meant, send JSON (`jsonify()`, `JsonResponse`) or `text/plain`.
- Never wrap request data in `Markup()`, `mark_safe()` or `SafeString()`.
<!-- end: how-to-fix -->

## Frameworks and APIs covered

- Flask
- Django
- FastAPI
- Starlette
- MarkupSafe
- bleach
- nh3

## Known limits

<!-- begin: known-limits -->
- A Flask view is recognised by its `route()`/`get()`/`post()` decorator in a module that imports
  Flask; class-based Flask views (`MethodView`) are not followed.
- A response body must be visibly text (a name, `+`, `%`, an f-string, `str()` or a string
  method). A helper that builds HTML from request data and returns it is not followed, while a
  call's result kept in a variable and returned is still taken for text.
- Values read from an object a call returned (a database row looked up by a request id) are taken
  for stored data, unless the call receives request data whole; a request value reaching such a
  call through a variable is missed.
- A Flask view returning the request's JSON whole is taken for JSON. A response whose content type
  is changed after it is made (`resp.mimetype = "text/plain"`) is still taken for HTML.
- Taint is not carried through a slice (`request.args["q"][:50]`).
- Request sources are recognised by their shape: a Flask `<int:n>` route parameter and a numeric
  Django URL argument still count as request data, and a function whose first parameter is named
  `request` in a Django module is taken for a view.
<!-- end: known-limits -->

## Tests

The test file [`rules/python/xss/xss.py`](../../../rules/python/xss/xss.py) holds every case the rule reports or accepts:
lines marked `ruleid:` must be reported and lines marked `ok:` must not. The known limits are
marked `todoruleid:` (missed) and `todook:` (wrongly reported). `npm test` runs them with OpenGrep,
and checks the example above as well.

The rule: [`rules/python/xss/xss.yml`](../../../rules/python/xss/xss.yml), added in version 2026.10.1.
